skill.name: cloudflare-one-migrations
skill.description: Plans migrations from Zscaler ZIA/ZPA, Palo Alto, legacy VPN, SWG, or SASE stacks to Cloudflare One. Use for migration assessments, policy mapping, rollout plans, and parity/gap analysis.
skill.summary: Builds accountable migration assessments and rollout plans for moving security stacks to Cloudflare One.
skill.author: cloudflare

content.value_statement: Legacy security policies often lack direct Cloudflare One equivalents. This skill builds an accountable migration map, staged rollout, validation plan, and rollback path.
actual_capabilities: Builds inventories from structured source exports, object files, logs, and hit counts.
Maps Zscaler, Palo Alto, VPN, SWG, and SASE resources to Cloudflare One targets.
Identifies prerequisites, unsupported behavior, partial mappings, and decisions requiring manual review.
Creates staged pilot, validation, rollback, and decommission plans.
Accounts for every source rule with its target, status, impact, and owner.
limitations: It does not deploy Cloudflare resources or install connectors.
Exact configuration requires current vendor documentation, API schemas, and complete source exports.
Some vendor behaviors have no direct Cloudflare One equivalent and require customer decisions.
Migration recommendations still require testing with real users, traffic, DNS, TLS, and logging.

use_cases.title: Assess a Zscaler migration
use_cases.description: Inventory ZIA and ZPA exports, map dependencies, and identify gaps before implementation.

use_cases.title: Translate Palo Alto policies
use_cases.description: Map rules, objects, zones, App-ID behavior, decryption, and GlobalProtect requirements into a reviewed migration plan.

use_cases.title: Govern a phased rollout
use_cases.description: Define pilots, validation gates, rollback ownership, source-rule accounting, and decommission criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Start a migration assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess our migration from [source stack] to Cloudflare One. List the exports, logs, identities, applications, policies, and connectivity details you need first.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner assessment with limited source information

prompt_templates.title: Build a policy mapping
prompt_templates.prompt: Using these [source exports], create a mapping table for Cloudflare One. Mark prerequisites, confidence, unsupported behavior, partial mappings, and manual decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Design a pilot rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a staged Cloudflare One pilot for [groups or sites]. Include dependency order, audit-mode defaults, validation gates, log comparisons, rollback steps, and owners.

prompt_templates.title: Audit migration completeness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this [migration plan] against the source exports. Account for every rule and dependency. Flag count mismatches, broad access, identity gaps, DNS conflicts, and unresolved exceptions.

output_examples.input: Assess a ZIA migration with incomplete URL category and identity exports.
output_examples.output: The assessment identifies missing category objects and SCIM data as blockers. It recommends completing exports before generating Gateway policies.

output_examples.input: Map a ZPA application segment with domains, CIDRs, connector groups, and bypass rules.
output_examples.output: The plan separates Access applications, tunnel routes, private DNS, reusable policies, and manual split-tunnel exclusions. It records egress and hostname-limit decisions.

output_examples.input: Create a pilot plan for two offices and a contractor group.
output_examples.output: The rollout starts with identity and connectivity dependencies, then audit-mode policies. Validation compares logs, tests access, and preserves an explicit rollback path.

best_practices: Provide structured source exports, object files, logs, and hit counts before requesting exact mappings.
Create dependencies first, then stage disabled or audit-mode rules for small pilot groups.
Review every partial, unsupported, unmapped, and manual item before enabling policies.
anti_patterns: Do not flatten zones, application identities, or vendor-specific behavior into generic lists.
Do not create broad allow-all rules to hide migration gaps.
Do not decommission source controls before pilot validation and rollback testing succeed.

faq.question: Which source platforms does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Zscaler ZIA and ZPA, Palo Alto platforms, legacy VPN, SWG, SD-WAN, and other SASE stacks.

faq.question: Does it deploy Cloudflare One configuration?
faq.answer: No. It produces assessments, mappings, rollout plans, and validation guidance.

faq.question: What inputs produce the best results?
faq.answer: Provide structured exports, policy objects, identities, connector data, logs, hit counts, and current architecture details.

faq.question: Can every source rule map directly?
faq.answer: No. Vendor-specific behavior may be partial, unsupported, or dependent on customer architecture decisions.

faq.question: How does it reduce migration risk?
faq.answer: It uses dependency ordering, audit-mode defaults, small pilots, count checks, log comparison, and explicit rollback steps.

faq.question: Does it replace security review?
faq.answer: No. Engineers must validate identity, DNS, routes, TLS inspection, DLP, application access, logging, and rollback behavior.
